transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, occupational health sent me, mostly. They seem to think I’m not eating enough. I mean, I’m functioning, I’m still getting through my days, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

Most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, and sometimes a few bites of chicken at night. A full meal just... it feels like I’m letting my standards slip, if that makes sense. I know that probably sounds odd.
Do you feel distressed or concerned about your eating habits, or has it started affecting other parts of your life, like work or relationships?

I wouldn’t say I’m... distressed exactly. I mean, I know that’s probably what people are worried about, but I’m trying to manage it.

It has caused some complications, I suppose. Occupational health hasn’t cleared me for field-related duties yet, and I can tell some of the team are wondering if I’m really fit to be out there. That’s hard to hear, honestly.

And socially, I’ve been avoiding meals with people. Not because I don’t like them, just... I don’t want the questions, or people watching what I’m eating and trying to push food on me. I know that probably doesn’t sound ideal.
Can you tell me if you have a fear of gaining weight, or if you do anything specific to try to keep from gaining weight, like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or using laxatives?

I wouldn’t say I’m doing anything extreme like that... but, yes, I suppose there is fear there.

If the scale is up even half a pound, I get this sort of jolt, like I’ve let things get away from me. Like I’ve lost control. And then I’ll usually cut back harder that day, just to correct it. I know that may sound a bit rigid, but I really can’t stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Do you feel like you are overweight, or do you have a strong fear of becoming overweight, even if others might say you’re at a healthy weight or even underweight?

I know people probably wouldn’t use the word overweight for me, and I’m not trying to be difficult about that. But yes… I do have a strong fear of it.

If the scale is up even half a pound, I get this jolt, like I’ve lost control somehow. Then I spend the day cutting back harder, just to get back on top of it. I know that’s not the most reasonable reaction, but I can’t really stand the idea of putting weight back on.
How long have you been feeling this way about food and weight?

I’m not completely sure I could put an exact date on it. It sort of crept up rather than starting all at once.

I mean, I’ve probably been more careful about food and weight for a while, but when it became this… preoccupying, I’m not sure. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s just been long enough that people have started noticing, I suppose. Does that answer what you mean?
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as larger than you actually are, or do you feel like you need to lose more weight even though others might say you’re already thin?

I wouldn’t say I see something completely different, exactly… but when I look in the mirror, I don’t really see what other people tell me they see.

I tend to go straight to my stomach, my waist, that area. If it doesn’t look lean enough, it can sort of ruin the whole day for me. I know that probably sounds vain or over the top, but it’s more like… I don’t feel right with myself. Like I can’t respect myself properly unless I look a certain way.

Does that make sense?
Do you tend to hold yourself to very high standards in other areas of your life, where even small mistakes or imperfections feel unacceptable to you?

I’m not sure. I mean… I’ve always tried to do things properly, especially at work, but I don’t know if I’d call it “unacceptable” exactly.

I don’t like making mistakes, no. I suppose most people don’t. I probably can be hard on myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. What kind of things do you mean?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition or another mental health issue that could explain some of these concerns about food or weight?

Not that I know of, no. I haven’t had anyone tell me there’s some medical reason for it, or another diagnosis that explains it.

I mean, I suppose I’ve not always been the best at bringing it up directly, so maybe I’m not giving you the perfect answer. But as far as I know, no… nothing like that. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Would you say your concerns about food and weight are mainly about trying to achieve or maintain a specific body shape or weight, even if others might not see it as necessary?

Yes… I think that’s probably fair.

I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m chasing some extreme thing, but it is very tied to how my body looks, especially my stomach and waist. I can look in the mirror and I just don’t see what other people say they see. I sort of measure the whole day by whether I look lean enough.

If I don’t, it feels like I’ve failed somehow… like I can’t really feel okay with myself or respect myself properly. I know that may not sound reasonable, but that’s how it tends to feel.

When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you feel like certain parts of your body, like your stomach or waist, appear larger than they actually are, or do you feel like you need to lose more weight even when you know you're already at a low weight?

Yes… I think so. I don’t know if I’d say it as confidently as “larger than they actually are,” because I don’t really know what they actually are, if that makes sense.

But when I look in the mirror, I don’t see what other people seem to be seeing. My eyes go straight to my stomach and waist, and if they don’t look lean enough, it sort of colors the whole day. I start feeling like I need to get it down more, or tighten it up somehow, even if someone else would probably say I don’t need to.

It’s embarrassing to say, but it can feel like whether I can respect myself depends on that. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking?
